science.title: Chromosome-level genome assembly of the parasitoid wasp Eretmocerus corni (Hymenoptera: Aphelinidae) for functional genomics and biological control research
science.description: Eretmocerus corni (Hymenoptera: Aphelinidae) is an economically and ecologically important parasitoid wasp widely used as a biological control agent against whitefly pests, including the greenhouse whitefly (Trialeurodes vaporariorum) and the sweetpotato whitefly (Bemisia tabaci). To enable research on its evolutionary biology, host-parasitoid interactions, and applied pest management, we present a high-quality chromosome-level genome assembly of E. corni. The assembly was generated using an integrated sequencing strategy combining Illumina short reads, PacBio continuous long reads (CLR), Oxford Nanopore long reads, and Hi-C chromatin interaction data. The final genome spans 778 Mb, with a scaffold N50 of 217.5 Mb and a BUSCO completeness of 94%. Repetitive sequences constitute 59.24% of the genome, and 22,725 protein-coding genes were annotated using a combination of de novo prediction, homology-based inference, and transcriptome data. The present comprehensive genomic resource provides a foundation for studying the genetic basis of parasitism, host specificity, and adaptive traits in parasitoid wasps. This dataset also supports functional genomics, evolutionary research, and the development of improved biological control strategies.

science.title: Dataset of lipidome and transcriptome of Gentiana crassicaulis seeds during artificial aging
science.description: Gentiana crassicaulis is a significant traditional medicinal plant in China. Currently, seed reproduction is the predominant method for large-scale seedling cultivation. However, the seeds of Gentiana are typically susceptible to aging and deterioration, which severely impacts seedling production and germplasm preservation. Research on the seed aging process of G. crassicaulis is still relatively limited, particularly in terms of systematic multi-omics data support. In this study, transcriptomic and lipidomic analyses were conducted on G. crassicaulis seeds artificially aged for 0, 5, 10, and 25 days. A total of 119.21 Gb of high-quality transcriptome sequencing data were generated, and 611 lipid molecular species across five major classes and 28 subclasses were comprehensively identified. This dataset provides a comprehensive multi-omics resource for investigating lipid metabolism and transcriptional regulation during seed aging in G. crassicaulis, which may facilitate future studies on germplasm conservation and seed quality improvement.
